speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing hematuria and right flank pain; can you describe exactly how the pain started and if it radiates anywhere?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Has the pain been sudden and severe, like a "kick in the side," or is it a dull ache? Additionally, have you noticed any blood clots in your urine or any nausea/vomiting?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy.
REQUEST TEST: Serum creatinine.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The urinalysis shows significant red blood cells and white blood cells, but negative nitrites suggest the infection might not be a simple cystitis. Does the pain move toward your groin or testicles, and do you notice any difficulty starting your urine stream or a feeling of incomplete emptying?

REQUEST TEST: Renal Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The ultrasound results were normal, which makes a large obstructing kidney stone less likely but does not rule out a smaller stone or a structural anomaly. Given your history of recurrent UTIs and the presence of white blood cells in your urine, have you experienced any fever or chills, and does the pain worsen when you drink fluids?

REQUEST TEST: Non-contrast CT KUB.
REQUEST IMAGES: Renal Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor

Since the CT KUB results are not available yet, have you noticed any "gravel" or small particles passing in your urine, or a history of kidney stones in your family? Also, do you have a history of smoking or use of NSAIDs?

text: I have already requested the Non-contrast CT KUB which is currently unavailable, so we must wait for that result to confirm or rule out a stone. In the meantime, given your recurrent UTIs and hematuria without a stone on ultrasound, could you tell me if you have a history of smoking or are currently taking NSAIDs? Also, have you noticed any abnormal urine color changes when your urine is fresh versus when it sits?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Renal Calculus (Kidney Stone) with secondary inflammation/infection.

The combination of sudden right flank pain, gross hematuria, and recurrent UTIs is highly suggestive of a kidney stone, even though the initial ultrasound was normal; we await the CT KUB results to confirm the presence of a radiolucent or small stone.
